podcast.title: Rusty Reunion (North by Northeast 2011)
podcast.body: Rusty reunited to perform at the North by Northeast Festival in April 2011 and has since maintained a loose relationship. "Rusty got back together for the North by Northeast Festival on April 2011 and have maintained a loose relationship ever since."

podcast.title: Ken MacNeil's Post-Rusty Career
podcast.body: After the band scattered, Ken MacNeil found work as a bricklayer and construction worker in Northern Ontario. "One of the guys, I think it was Ken. Found a job as a bricklayer and construction worker in Northern Ontario."

podcast.body: Scott McCullough teamed up with singer Ken MacNeil in Toronto, gathered a full band, and began recording independent records. "He teamed up with singer Ken McNeil in Toronto, pulled a full group around them, and started recording indie records."

xref.title: Recovery and Rejoining Red Hot Chili Peppers (1996-1998)
xref.body: John Frusciante quit heroin cold turkey in late 1996, after five years of constant use, though he continued using crack for a couple more years. In January 1998, a friend convinced him to seriously enter rehab. He faced a lethal mouth infection requiring all his rotted teeth to be pulled out and replaced with $75,000 worth of implants to prevent sepsis, as well as skin grafts for abscesses on his arms. After rehab worked, Anthony Kiedis reached out to him at a gallery event showcasing his paintings, and Flea personally invited him to rejoin the band. Frusciante, who didn't even own a guitar, was bought a '62 Stratocaster by Kiedis. The band reassembled in Flea's garage in September 1998, where they began jamming, writing, and recording demos, including an early version of "Californication." "John was rusty both physically and mentally. They started jamming and they started writing."

xref.title: Death Details - March 12, 2024
xref.body: Rusty Wilson died on March 12, 2024, at the age of 62. His cause of death was meningitis. "He was 62 when he was claimed by men in Gytus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Background as Bar-Bouncer
xref.body: Rusty Wilson was an ex-bar-bouncer before being recruited by Tom Wilson to become the bass player for the Canadian band Junkhouse. "He was an ex-bar-bouncer who was recruited by Tom Wilson, in relation to be junkhouse's bass player."
